name: INIU P62 20000 mAh 65 W power bank
summary: A USB-C power bank documented as P62-E1, held in draft while its Canadian safety evidence and exact listing configuration are reviewed.
description: This is a candidate for a device-specific USB charging kit, not an AC power station replacement. Check the device charging profile and shared-port limits before choosing a setup. The owner-reported P62 identifier agrees with a manufacturer P62-E1 page, but advertised protection features do not independently establish certification of the selected Canadian listing.

specs.label: Advertised cell capacity
specs.value: 20000 mAh; usable USB-delivered capacity not independently measured

specs.label: Maximum single USB-C output
specs.value: 65 W on USB-C1; compatible device and cable required

specs.label: Shared output
specs.value: USB-C1 + USB-C2: 45 W + 20 W; three ports: 60 W total

specs.label: Display and cable
specs.value: Digital charge display; manufacturer describes a detachable USB-C GoCord

pros: USB-C input and output support a compact device-charging kit.
A digital indicator makes the reported charge level visible.
cons: 65 W is not available independently from every port at once.
Cell mAh is not a measured phone recharge count.
Canadian certification evidence for this exact unit has not been independently verified.
useCases: Evaluate compatible phone and laptop charging profiles after safety review.
Plan a compact communications charging kit with separately checked cables.

confirmed.text: The manufacturer identifies P62-E1 with 20000 mAh capacity and 65 W maximum USB-C output.
The reviewed manufacturer and CPSC recall identifies specific BI-B41 batches, not P62-E1.

unverifiedClaims: Owner-transcribed seller claims include overcharge protection, short-circuit protection and a 3-year warranty; not independently verified.
The owner describes an integrated cable; the manufacturer describes a detachable GoCord. Confirm the supplied configuration.
safetyNotes: No independent Canadian certification record or test report for this exact listing was obtained. Marketing safety badges are not treated as certification evidence.
The BI-B41 notice is a different-model recall; it neither proves P62-E1 is recalled nor certifies P62-E1 as safe.
No INIU/P62/P62-E1 exact match was identified in the downloaded Health Canada summary dataset; absence is not a safety clearance.
